signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: CHF outperforms across the G10 board with a 1W average gain of +1.625% across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at -1.079% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 2.704% bilateral spread. RBA 4.85% vs SNB 0.00% delivers a massive +485bp nominal carry advantage to AUD (+362bp on an OIS basis), but safe-haven demand and VIX elevated at 30.4 completely override the carry return. AUD/USD sits extended 4.2 ATR below its 20-day moving average in a clear downtrend, while AUD/CHF trades at 0.5495, holding below its moving average cluster. BEER model misvaluation highlights AUD/CHF as cheap at z=-2.31σ (spot 0.5495 vs fair value 0.5588), but structural risk-off flows continue to push spot away from equilibrium. Trade bias: Short AUD/CHF, momentum-driven bilateral G10 divergence. Catalyst: Australia Private New Capital Expenditure data at 00:30 UTC. Risk: VIX falls back below 20, triggering a rapid unwinding of CHF safe-haven flows back into carry.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Hawkish BoE Repricing + Technical Resiliency
signals.text: BoE Governor Bailey and MPC member Mann delivered aggressive comments, stating it is more likely than not that rates must rise further if energy prices stay elevated, while Mann urged hiking rates more and sooner. BoE 4.00% (HIKING) matches Fed 4.00% (ON HOLD), leaving the OIS SONIA-SOFR spread neutral at -6bp. GBP/USD trades at 1.3116, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3279/1.3285/1.3398) inside a counter-trend pullback within a broader downtrend structure. Leveraged funds hold net long +23,730 contracts (pctl 38, z -0.29) while retail sentiment shows 78% long, reflecting broad positioning support despite recent price weakness. Options markets show a mild put skew with 25d RR at -0.59 while 1M IV runs at 6.5% vs HV30 at 5.9% (+0.6% VRP). Trade bias: Long GBP/USD, central bank hawkish repricing setup. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI data release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Extended risk-off equity liquidation forces liquidity-driven USD buying.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Crowded Carry vs Options Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.95, holding just below the key 160.00 level that has historically drawn verbal intervention warnings from the MoF. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% provides a +275bp rate spread (+269bp OIS carry premium), keeping the pair structurally bid, but elevated VIX at 30.4 compresses risk appetite. 25-Delta Risk Reversals print a strong put skew at -1.82, showing institutional options traders actively paying up for downside JPY protection despite JPY COT leveraged funds net short at -29,545 contracts (pctl 85, z +1.12). Cross-asset correlations show USD/JPY vs VIX at corr=-0.071 vs 252d norm=+0.269 (z=-2.28σ), confirming a breakdown in JPY's standard safe-haven transmission during equity sell-offs. Technical structure shows USD/JPY in a tight range box around SMA20 at 158.75 and SMA200 at 158.82. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY while holding above 158.00 support. Catalyst: Japan Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: MoF executes direct market intervention or VIX spikes above 35, triggering systemic carry unwinds.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme vs Speculative Positioning Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5489, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5557/0.5617/0.5795) in a firm technical downtrend extended 2.04σ below BEER model fair value (spot 0.5489 vs fair value 0.5556). Conversely, CFTC COT leveraged funds hold net short -23,862 contracts (long% 25.3%, pctl 23), showing institutional money positioned for ongoing weakness while retail attempts to catch a falling knife. Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75% provides a +125bp carry advantage to USD, keeping structural pressure on the kiwi. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, riding institutional momentum against retail extreme. Catalyst: RBNZ Bulletin release at 01:30 UTC. Risk: Short-covering rally triggered by broader USD weakness following US GDP/PCE releases.
